info.title: Sustain API
info.description:
Sustain's API: monitors, incidents, status pages, alerts and reports, for the workspace whose address it is on.

Sign in with an API token an Admin makes in Settings › API tokens, as a bearer token: it acts as the person who made it, with their role now. Every answer has the request's id in its `X-Request-Id` header, and every refusal is an `Error` with a stable code. Times are ISO 8601 in UTC.

`/api/v1` keeps its meaning: a field may be added to an answer, and an optional one to a request, but nothing is taken away or changed in meaning. See docs/OPENAPI.md.

critical.description: Whether it pages out of its client's support hours where a policy pages for critical services alone (docs/ALERT_ROUTING.md).

contract.description: Its own contract, in place of its client's; null when it follows its client's.

monitors.description: Its monitors now, in the order they joined.

depends_on.description: The services it depends on, by id (docs/SERVICES.md).

status_mode.description: How it's shown: by its monitors and what it depends on (automatic), as set by hand (manual), or as set unless those say worse (hybrid).

manual_status.description: The status set by hand; null for `automatic`.

SecretSettings.description: A new secret's name and value: the value is sealed at once and never shown again.

SecretKept.description: A value monitors' requests are made with that must stay private, as the API shows it: never its value.

id.description: What a monitor names it by: its `secret_reference`.

version.description: Rises each time it's given a new value.

ClientSettings.description: A client: a company of the directory by Link's id, or a new company Link makes first.

ClientKept.description: A client: a company in the organisation's directory at Link, kept by Link's id and read live, with its services and its status page.

company_id.description: Its company at Link, by Link's id; null once Link erased it.

support_hours.description: When its own service desk answers, by which policies' rules alert; null for none.

contract.description: What its services' availability is held to in its reports; null for none.

AlertPolicyKept.description: Who a monitor's or a service's alerts reach, and when.

is_default.description: The default has every monitor and service no other policy lists, and can't be deleted.

contact_ids.description: The alert contacts it alerts, or null for every one.

channel_ids.description: The channels it alerts, or null for every one.

schedule_ids.description: The on-call schedules whose person on call it alerts too.

delay_seconds.description: How long a monitor must stay down before anyone is alerted.

remind_seconds.description: How often to remind while it stays down; null for never.

remind_limit.description: How many reminders at most, or null for every one until someone takes it or it recovers.

notify_recovery.description: Whether recoveries are sent, or left out.

monitor_ids.description: The monitors it applies to, taken from any other policy; none for the default, which has the rest.

service_ids.description: The services it applies to, and their monitors no policy lists, in the same way.

client_ids.description: The clients it applies to, their services and monitors no policy lists, in the same way.

page_major_only.description: A rule, Enterprise's: only a major outage pages; a partial outage or a degradation goes to its chat and webhook channels and its contacts alone.

critical_only_out_of_hours.description: A rule, Enterprise's: out of a client's support hours, only its critical services page; the rest go to its chat and webhook channels and its contacts alone.

in_hours_contact_ids.description: A rule, Enterprise's: the alert contacts it tells instead, paging no one, in a client's support hours; none for no such rule.

in_hours_channel_ids.description: The channels it tells instead in a client's support hours.

client_recipient_ids.description: Enterprise's: a client's own people it alerts, each confirmed by email first, by Sustain's ids for them.

in_hours_client_recipient_ids.description: A client's own people it tells instead in a client's support hours.

AlertChannelSettings.description: An alert channel to add, by its kind: a webhook's, Slack's, Discord's or Teams's address (`url`); PagerDuty's or Opsgenie's key (`key`) and region; or a Telegram bot's token (`key`) and the chat it posts to (`chat_id`). A webhook may also be sent events besides alerts (`events`): incidents', maintenance's and monitors', none unless named.

url.description: A webhook's, Slack's, Discord's or Teams's address.

key.description: PagerDuty's or Opsgenie's integration key, or a Telegram bot's token.

region.description: PagerDuty's or Opsgenie's account's region; us unless given.

chat_id.description: A Telegram chat's id, or a public channel's @name.

AlertChannelKept.description: Somewhere alerts are sent beside email, and how its deliveries are going: never its address, only its host.

events.description: A webhook's: the events besides alerts it's sent too, incidents', maintenance's and monitors'; none for any other.

signing_secret.description: What a webhook's deliveries are signed with; only a webhook has one.

AlertContactSettings.description: An alert contact to add: one of the workspace's people, or an address that confirms first.

AlertContactKept.description: An address alerts are emailed to once it's confirmed: one of the workspace's people, or another an Admin added.

user_id.description: For one of the workspace's people, their account, whose address it is; null for any other address.

weekly_report.description: Whether they get the weekly report, once confirmed: on unless they or an Admin turned it off.

time_zone.description: An IANA time zone, such as Europe/London.

first_shift.description: When the first shift starts, in its time zone, such as 2026-10-12T09:00.

from.description: When it's on from, each day, as HH:MM.

until.description: When it's on until, each day, as HH:MM.

OnCallScheduleKept.description: Some of the workspace's people, on call in turn by the clock in its time zone, and who is on call now.

when_nobody.description: Whom it alerts when nobody's on call: wait, holding an alert while it is off until it is on again; contacts, every confirmed contact; or people, those it names. With nobody left on its rota, wait alerts every contact.

fallback_user_ids.description: The people it alerts when nobody's on call, with people: none otherwise.

time_zone.description: An IANA time zone, such as Europe/London.

first_shift.description: When the first shift starts, in its time zone, as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM.

shift_length.description: How many of `shift_unit` a shift lasts.

on_duty.description: When it's on; null for all the time.

user_ids.description: The rota: the workspace's people, by their ids, in turn.

StatusPageSettings.description: A page of its own: its name, which is its title, and what it shows, those placed on it unless it says otherwise.

StatusPageKept.description: One of a workspace's status pages: its own, at the workspace's address, or a page of its own on a domain named to it.

name.description: Its title: the workspace's name for its own page.

own.description: Whether it is the workspace's own page, at the workspace's address and on any domain that names no page.

shows.description: Every public service and monitor, placed or not, or only those placed on it.

client_id.description: The client whose page it is, showing its public services as they come and go; null for any other.

access.description: Who may open it: anyone, or only those let in (docs/PRIVATE_PAGES.md).

email_domains.description: The email domains at which anyone may sign in to it by an emailed link.

client_contacts.description: Whether a client's page lets in its client's contacts at Link, by an emailed link.

password_set.description: Whether it has a password, never what it is.

time_zone.description: The IANA time zone its times are shown in, as Europe/London; null for each reader's own.

indexed.description: Whether search engines may list it; a private page is never listed, whatever this says.

language.description: The language its own words are in; what the team writes is shown as written. English unless set.

colour.description: Its own colour, # and six lower-case hex digits, for its buttons, links and initial, shown darker in light and lighter in dark where it would be hard to read; null for Sustain's own.

description.description: A sentence or two beneath its name, 300 characters at most; null for none.

RepeatingMaintenanceSettings.description: Repeating maintenance to make: on which days, from what time by which time zone's clocks, for how long, what to say, and what it covers.

RepeatingMaintenanceKept.description: Maintenance on the same days of every week, at the same time by its time zone's clocks: each time a window of its own, made two weeks ahead.

message.description: What the status page says about each of its times.

days.description: The days it starts on, Monday first: mon to sun.

start_time.description: When it starts on each, by its time zone's clocks: 02:00.

time_zone.description: An IANA time zone, as Europe/London.

monitor_ids.description: The monitors it covers, or null for every one.

service_ids.description: The services it covers, with their monitors; none when it covers every monitor.

client_ids.description: The clients it covers, with the services each has as each time runs.

PrivateLocationSettings.description: A private location's name: once each whatever its case, 60 characters at most.

PrivateLocationKept.description: One of the workspace's own agents, run inside its own network, which checks its monitors there for it alone (docs/PRIVATE_LOCATIONS.md): never its key.

key_prefix.description: Enough of its key to tell it from another.

key_made_at.description: When its key was made: its agent asks with no other.

key.description: `sw_location_<region>_`, the workspace's id as hex, `_` and 48 hex digits: its agent's `SUSTAIN_LOCATION_KEY`.

Refused.description: Refused: the request, or who made it, isn't one the API takes.

Unavailable.description: Sustain couldn't answer; it is safe to ask again.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Your key for this request, its caller's own: sent again with the same request within a day, it's answered as it was the first time, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, and not made twice. With another request it's refused, `422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; while the first is still being answered, `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_USE`.

session.name: sustain_session
session.description: A person signed in to the console with their Optymyse account.

apiToken.description: An API token an Admin made in Settings › API tokens. It acts as the person who made it.

ingestToken.description: An ingest token, which can only add log lines.
